Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Valerie Cole, DOB: 19/09/1993, Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 64 Cliveden Place, South Wimbledon
- Referring GP: Dr Smith, Practice: Babylon, Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Adjustment disorder with anxiety (work-related) — consistent with transcript and DDx (High likelihood)
- Secondary: Generalized anxiety disorder (provisional) — possible if symptoms persist beyond diagnostic timeframe (Medium likelihood)
- Tertiary: Acute situational panic-type symptoms / paroxysmal anxiety episodes (situational panic attacks) — consider medical exclusion for paroxysmal cardiac arrhythmia (e.g., SVT/AF) (Medium likelihood for arrhythmia per DDx; psychiatric formulation: situational panic)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: None documented
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: Not recorded (patient reports no chronic medical conditions in transcript)

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: None reported
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): No prior psychiatric treatment reported; has not attended therapy previously
- Family History: Mother has history of depression

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with parents
- Social Support: Good family support; talks with mother who suggested GP contact
- Occupation/Education: Employed at a fashion retailer head office; started this new job ~2 months ago; reports difficult relationship with boss
- Alcohol Use: Social alcohol; increased intake on Fridays/Saturdays and occasional drinking during week; patient states possibly "quite a lot" at weekends
- Smoking/Substance Use: Occasional smoking; denies recreational drug use
- Key Stressors: Recent new stressful job (hostile boss, performance worries), commuting/public transport (tube) anxiety, work-focused life with limited leisure time

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Cooperative, engaged with consultation, coherent and relevant responses (phone consult); no abnormal psychomotor activity documented
- Mood & Affect: Describes being anxious and "down"; affect congruent with reported mood
- Speech & Thought: Speech coherent and goal-directed; no formal thought disorder documented; no ruminative content beyond excessive worry about work
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbances reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented to self and able to confirm name/DOB/address (orientation to person/place/time inferred from responses)
- Attention/Concentration: Not formally assessed; patient reports daytime fatigue and reduced enjoyment which may impair concentration (difficulty concentrating not directly documented)
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Good insight — recognizes problem, sought GP, willing to engage in talking therapy

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Difficulty initiating sleep, lying awake for hours, shallow sleep; estimates ~3–4 hours/night; early-morning awakening with palpitations before alarm
- Appetite: No significant change; increased chocolate intake reported
- Motivation/Energy: Low energy, anhedonia, reduced participation in previously enjoyed activities (running, tennis)
- Anxiety Symptoms: Morning panic/dread about leaving house and work, racing/irregular palpitations lasting minutes up to ~10 minutes, avoidance of social activities, heightened anxiety on public transport

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denies suicidal ideation; no self-harm reported; no risk to others identified
- Protective Factors: Good family support, insight, willingness to engage in therapy, continued attendance at work
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (based on denial of suicidal ideation and presence of support)
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Family history of depression (mother); possible baseline vulnerability to mood/anxiety difficulties.
- Precipitating factors: Starting a new, stressful job ~2 months ago with perceived hostile boss and stressful commute; temporal association with symptom onset.
- Perpetuating factors: Avoidance of social/leisure activities, poor sleep, increased alcohol use at weekends, reduced exercise, rumination about work performance; ongoing exposure to the workplace stressor.
- Protective factors: Supportive family, insight, willingness to engage in psychological treatment, continued functioning at work (has not taken time off).
- Medical considerations: Prominent irregular, paroxysmal palpitations warrant basic medical investigations (ECG/ambulatory monitoring and blood tests including thyroid function, FBC) to exclude arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, anemia or other reversible causes as per DDx. Psychological presentation most consistent with adjustment disorder with anxiety but GAD and medical causes remain possible.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Adjustment disorder with anxiety (work-related)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce morning anxiety and dread about leaving the house
  - Improve sleep to feel rested and regain enjoyment in activities
  - Manage workplace-related stress and improve day-to-day functioning
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Reduce anxiety symptoms and functional impairment
  - Provide prompt psychological support (talking therapy) and self-help resources
  - Exclude medical causes of palpitations (arrhythmia, thyroid dysfunction, anemia)
- Actions (Patient):
  - Self-refer or accept referral to NHS talking therapy (IAPT) as discussed
  - Access recommended online CBT-based resources while awaiting therapy
  - Call support line/clinic to arrange basic blood tests as advised by clinician
  - Implement sleep hygiene measures and attempt gradual re-engagement with exercise and social activities
  - Monitor and document palpitations (timing, duration, triggers) and seek urgent care if chest pain, syncope, or severe breathlessness occur
  - Reduce alcohol intake, especially at weekends; avoid excessive nicotine/stimulants near bedtime
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide self-referral link/resources for talking therapy and online CBT materials (documented in notes)
  - Arrange basic blood tests: FBC, TSH/FT4, and other baseline bloods as clinically indicated (GP recommended tests)
  - Arrange follow-up appointment approximately 1 week after blood tests to review results and reassess symptoms
  - Consider 12-lead ECG at initial assessment; if palpitations persist or ECG abnormal, arrange ambulatory monitoring (e.g., Holter) and cardiology referral
  - If insufficient response to psychological interventions or if symptoms escalate, consider pharmacotherapy (e.g., short-term SSRI or targeted anxiolytic) after shared decision-making and assessment of risks/benefits
  - Provide written information on sleep hygiene, panic management techniques, and crisis contacts

Secondary Problem: Generalized anxiety disorder (provisional)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce pervasive worry and restore ability to enjoy activities
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Monitor symptom duration and severity; if symptoms persist ≥6 months or impair function despite therapy, treat as GAD
- Actions (Patient):
  - Engage consistently with psychological therapy and self-help strategies
  - Track symptom duration and functional impact, report persistence to GP
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Reassess at follow-up; if criteria for GAD met or symptoms persist, consider referral to secondary mental health services and discuss evidence-based pharmacotherapy (e.g., SSRI) and structured CBT

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Nature of situational/work-related anxiety and talking therapy (IAPT) referral/self-referral process
  - Sleep hygiene and basic strategies to improve sleep
  - Explanation that palpitations are commonly anxiety-related but require basic blood tests and possible ECG to exclude medical causes
  - When to seek urgent help (increasing panic attacks, inability to cope, suicidal thoughts, chest pain, fainting)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increasing frequency/intensity of panic episodes or palpitations
  - Inability to attend work or severe social withdrawal
  - New or worsening suicidal thoughts or self-harm ideation
  - Progressive insomnia or marked functional decline
- Coping Strategies:
  - Breathing and grounding techniques for acute anxiety
  - Sleep hygiene (consistent bedtime routine, limit alcohol/caffeine, reduce screen time)
  - Gradual behavioural activation (resume exercise, social contact)
  - Use of online CBT modules and support helplines; discuss worries with trusted family/friends

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal consent documented during consultation)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded (patient to self-refer to NHS talking therapy/IAPT)
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Planned follow-up ~1 week after completion/results of basic blood tests (to be arranged)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Adjustment disorder with anxiety (High) — Clear temporal relation to starting a new stressful job ~2 months ago with symptoms focused on work and marked functional impairment (DDx: High likelihood).
- Generalized anxiety disorder (Medium) — Symptoms of excessive worry, insomnia and impairment fit GAD, but current duration (~2 months) is below 6-month threshold (DDx: Medium likelihood).
- Acute situational panic-type reaction / situational panic attacks (Medium) — Episodic intense anxiety and paroxysmal palpitations related to work/commute stress; medical causes (paroxysmal arrhythmia) need exclusion (DDx: situational panic likely; arrhythmia possible).

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs, 12-lead ECG and ambulatory monitoring results: Not recorded / not performed
  - Blood test results (FBC, thyroid function, other labs): Not recorded / not yet done
  - Formal suicide risk screening scores/scales: Not recorded
  - Medication doses (no psychotropic meds currently prescribed): Not applicable
  - Written copy of plan handed to patient: Not recorded
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - No direct conflicts; DDx expands differential to include medical causes (arrhythmia, thyroid dysfunction, anemia) which align with symptoms described in transcript and were recommended for exclusion by GP.
● Transcript quality notes:
  - Consultation was a telephone/remote consult; no physical examination or vital signs recorded.
  - Dialogue is largely complete and coherent; a few brief clinician prompt lines were truncated but clinical content adequate.
  - Objective clinical investigations recommended (blood tests, ECG) were not yet performed during this consult.
